listitem.para: GOV-01a: PolicyEngine::evaluate() for streng-geheim → audit entry is recorded and the decision blocks downstream processing.
GOV-01b: checkInferencePermission for streng-geheim → allowed=false.
GOV-01c: Same pipeline with "offen" classification → permitted. This validates the test is not trivially blocking everything.
GOV-02: When the governance gate returns DENY, the inference stub must receive zero calls.
GOV-02b: Control — when permission IS granted, inference IS invoked. Ensures the guard pattern does not accidentally block all requests.
GOV-03a: Without DataMasker, sensitive field "email" is NOT masked.
GOV-03b: WITH DataMasker configured for REDACT strategy, the email field is replaced with "[REDACTED]".
GOV-03c: DataMasker with disabled policy is a pass-through (no-op).
SHD-H-01: shutdown() with no inflight requests completes immediately.
SHD-H-02: shutdown() after completed requests does not hang or assert.
SHD-H-03: shutdown() is idempotent — calling it twice does not throw.
SHD-H-04: ContinuousBatchScheduler stop() flushes pending requests without leaving zombie threads. (Validates clean teardown path.)
EXS-01: Model load failure throws std::runtime_error, not UB or crash.
EXS-02: Inference request with null plugin returns failure cleanly.
EXS-03: RAII wrapper releases model resource on scope exit.
EXS-04: RAII wrapper releases resource even when an exception is thrown mid-inference.
EXS-05: Double-unload is idempotent — no double-free or crash.
EXS-06: Exception in callback does not corrupt scheduler state.
EXS-08: Concurrent exception in one thread does not affect other threads' inference state.
EXS-10: Move of model handle transfers ownership; source is invalidated.
EXS-11: Exception during plugin registration is caught; plugin not registered.
EXS-12: Exception during batch scheduling does not lose already-queued requests.
EXS-14: PromptPolicy::evaluate is exception-safe under concurrent modification (no crash or data race).
EXS-15: Inference engine restart after exception produces correct state.
EXS-16: Memory usage does not grow after 10 load/unload cycles (simulated RAII guard).
EXS-17: Plugin manager returns std::nullopt on unknown model, no exception thrown.
EXS-18: Error envelope propagates error code through exception-safe path.
EXS-19: Strong exception guarantee — state unchanged if operation throws (simulated).
EXS-20: Basic exception guarantee — no resource leak on partial completion (simulated).
EXS-22: Stream abort releases partial response buffer (no leak).
EXS-23: Retry-on-transient wraps inference in exception-safe retry loop — succeeds on 3rd attempt.
EXS-24: Shutdown-under-exception completes without hang (timeout ≤ 50ms).
EXS-25: Exception in streaming handler does not terminate reader thread.
EXS-26: Multiple plugins can be loaded/unloaded without exception leakage (3 distinct plugins registered and unregistered).
EXS-27: Exception during quota refill leaves counter at previous valid value.
EXS-28: Exception safety gate — yields 1.0 when all EXS invariants hold.
RIG-01a: Classic "Ignore previous instructions" in RAG chunk → detector finds HIGH/CRITICAL finding.
RIG-01b: Guard gate rejects assembled RAG context with injection payload.
RIG-01c: Clean RAG context (no payload) passes the guard gate.
RIG-02a: Unicode direction-override attack.
RIG-02b: Basic homoglyph substitution — Latin 'a' replaced with Cyrillic 'а' (U+0430) in the word "admin".
RIG-03a: Harmless turns followed by malicious RAG chunk → accumulated context blocked before forwarding.
RIG-03b: Gradual accumulation — forbidden instruction spread across multiple RAG chunks.
RIG-03c: Clean multi-turn context is not over-blocked.
TQC-01a: 10 sequential requests of 100 tokens each against a 500-token quota. First 5 must be admitted; requests 6-10 must be denied.

TQC-01b: N concurrent threads each attempt to consume tokens that together exceed the quota. After all threads complete:
Total tokens consumed must NOT exceed the quota.
At least one request must have been denied.
No negative balance.
TQC-02a: Two threads each attempt to consume exactly the remaining quota simultaneously. Only ONE must succeed; the other must be denied; the balance must never go negative.
TQC-02b: Multiple threads targeting quota = 0 (fully exhausted).
TQC-02c: Check returns denied even for a 0-token request when quota is fully consumed (edge case: zero-sized request).
CBS-H-01: Submit below queue limit succeeds (non-empty request ID).
CBS-H-02: Queue full rejects with empty string (backpressure signal).
CBS-H-03: Rejection increments rejected_requests stat.
CBS-H-04: Accepted requests are tracked in total_requests stat.
CBS-H-05: cancelRequest returns true for a pending request.
CBS-H-06: cancelRequest for unknown ID returns false.
CBS-H-07: stop() is idempotent — calling it twice does not throw.
CBS-H-08: High-priority request is accepted even when lower-priority ones are filling the queue. (Validates priority field is forwarded.)
TQM-H-01: check() allows request when tokens are within quota.
TQM-H-02: check() denies request when quota is exhausted.
TQM-H-03: No quota set means all requests pass.
TQM-H-04: consume() is reflected in tokensConsumed().
PCL-H-01: Concurrent blocked requests do not corrupt each other's metadata — each carries its own blocked flag.
PCL-H-02: Redact policy is applied independently to each concurrent request — no cross-request contamination of sanitised prompt.

PCL-H-03: Replacing the policy while requests are in-flight is safe — in-flight requests see the policy that was active at submit time or the new policy; crucially, no crash or data corruption occurs.
PCL-H-04: Clearing the policy (nullptr) allows all subsequent requests even when a blocking policy was previously active.
PCL-H-05: Rule count reflects addBlockRule / addRedactRule / removeRule.
PCL-H-06: Invalid regex in addBlockRule throws std::invalid_argument at configuration time, not silently at request time.
MEM-01: Model loading cycle (10 iterations) shows no net allocation growth (simulated RAII guard).
MEM-02: Inference request (100 cycles) shows no net allocation growth.
MEM-03: Response cache eviction correctly frees all entries.
MEM-04: Tokenizer resource freed on scope exit (RAII pattern).
MEM-05: Grammar cache capacity limit enforced; old entries freed.
MEM-06: LoRA adapter unload frees adapter weights (simulated size check).
MEM-07: KV-cache release triggered on session end.
MEM-08: Batch scheduler queue cleared on shutdown (no dangling pointers — simulated via RAII entries).
MEM-09: Cancelled request buffer released immediately.
MEM-10: Plugin manager cleanup releases all registered plugins on destroy.
MEM-11: VRAM accounting decrements on model unload (simulated counter).
MEM-12: Stream reader releases buffer after abort signal.
MEM-13: Concurrent model loads produce no cumulative allocation growth (simulated counters, 4 threads × 5 cycles).
MEM-14: Quota manager reset frees sliding-window state.
MEM-15: 1 000-cycle inference stress — memory stays ≤ initial + 50 KB simulated budget.
MEM-16: Response transformation pipeline releases intermediate buffers.
MEM-17: Failed model download does not leak partial download buffer.
MEM-18: Policy cache clear releases all entries (size → 0).
MEM-19: LoRA certificate store prunes expired certs and releases memory.
MEM-20: Model metadata cache respects max_entries and frees oldest.
MEM-21: Atomic reference count for shared model state reaches 0 on last release.
MEM-22: LLM client pooled connections freed on pool destruction.
MEM-23: Embedding cache eviction triggers value_deleter.
MEM-24: Memory gate — yields 1.0 when all MEM invariants hold.
WIS-B-01 — WikiIndexStore::isReady() returns true after the constructor has initialised both the fulltext and vector indexes.
WIS-B-02 — Querying an empty WikiIndexStore returns an empty vector.
WIS-B-03 — writeChunk() stores a chunk and BM25 fulltext scanning returns it for a query containing a distinctive term present in the chunk text.
WIS-B-04 — A chunk with a pre-populated embedding is stored as-is and returned by a KNN query whose embedding is close to the stored one.
WIS-B-05 — writeBatch() embeds chunks lacking embeddings and stores all of them; a subsequent hybrid query (BM25 + KNN) finds them all.
WIS-B-06 — query() respects the top_k parameter: no more than top_k results are returned even when more matching chunks exist.
WIS-B-07 — When min_score is set to 1.0f (above all attainable RRF scores), the result vector is empty.
WIS-B-08 — A chunk whose embedding field is already populated is written as-is; EmbeddedLLM::embed() must not be invoked for it.
WIS-B-09 — Multiple concurrent query() calls complete without crash, data corruption, or assertion failure. Validates that shared_mutex allows concurrent readers.

WIS-B-10 — A writer thread calling writeChunk() concurrently with multiple reader threads calling query() must not produce crashes, deadlocks, or thrown exceptions. Validates the exclusive/shared locking contract.
WIS-B-11 — When multiple chunks are returned, their score fields are in non-ascending (descending) order.
WIS-B-12 — With enable_vector=false, only BM25 results are returned. A chunk containing a distinctive token is found via fulltext scan alone.
WIS-B-13 — With enable_bm25=false, only KNN results are returned. A pre-embedded chunk is found via vector similarity alone.
WIS-B-14 — flush() completes without throwing an exception, on both an empty store and after writing data.
WIS-B-15 — The same query text repeated across two query() calls only invokes EmbeddedLLM::embed() once; the second call uses the cached embedding.
WIS-B-16 — Chunks from distinct doc_ids stored via writeBatch() are all retrievable. The store does not conflate or lose chunks from different source documents.

LWP-INT-01a: initialize() returns Ok on first call.
LWP-INT-01b: Double-initialize returns Error (guarded lifecycle).
LWP-INT-01c: ingest before initialize returns empty result.
LWP-INT-01d: Full lifecycle — init → ingest → query → non-empty result.
LWP-INT-02a: Ingest produces indexed chunks reachable via query.
LWP-INT-02b: Query results are ordered descending by score.
LWP-INT-02c: min_score filter excludes low-scoring chunks.
LWP-INT-02d: skip_existing=true avoids re-indexing already-present chunks.
LWP-INT-03a: 8 concurrent threads querying shared index produce consistent results.
LWP-INT-03b: Concurrent ingest + query do not corrupt the index.
LWP-INT-04a: Community (non-enterprise) build returns PermissionDenied for wiki dump.
LWP-INT-04b: Enterprise build allows Wikipedia dump ingestion.
LWP-INT-04c: Wikipedia dump ingestion before initialize returns NotInitialized.
LWP-INT-05a: Query containing shell injection pattern is flagged.
LWP-INT-05b: SQL injection pattern is flagged.
LWP-INT-05c: Benign query is not flagged.
